title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
This page has no written mathematics. It is the banner sheet of an IBM-style mainframe print job: '//* FATAR 0338', large block characters '0002' and 'FATAR', and the trailer '****A END JOB 338 FATAR ROOM 3.01.58 PM 19 AUG 82 R6.PR1 SYS JES2'. Grothendieck reused it as scrap paper and drew over it in brown, orange and teal felt-tip. The archivist's page number is '98'.

The drawings are discs (circles or ovals) cut by chords or arcs that end on the boundary circle. Many arcs carry small tick marks where they meet the boundary. Some regions are hatched:
- The large orange disc is cut by nearly straight crossing lines. These bound hatched triangular regions, and some lines run outside the circle.
- Several brown discs are cut by curved arcs. Their hatched regions sit near the top, and some arcs are dashed.
- Two thin-pen discs (lower right) carry chords meeting at interior points. They show a hatched triangle near the centre and thick orange segments marking a portion of the boundary circle.
- A teal-filled disc carries a dense network of curves converging toward a central region.

In the context of the dossier ('Chirurgie des surfaces conformes'), these are plausibly heuristic pictures of conformal or hyperbolic structures on a disc. Possible readings:
- geodesics in the Klein model (straight chords) and the Poincaré model (circular arcs);
- geodesic triangles or polygons cut out by such geodesics, with the hatching marking a chosen face;
- marked boundary intervals (orange arcs), perhaps for a bordered surface or for reflection and real-structure arguments;
- dissections of a disc into cells, i.e. the 'surgery' (cutting and regluing) of conformal surfaces.

The neighbouring pages discuss real structures on complex elliptic curves. They treat the dihedral automorphism groups D_n (n = 2, 4, 6) with the square and hexagon cases, and the parameter a(σ) = Q(e_-)/Q(e_+) with a(−σ) = 1/a(σ). The written argument runs continuously from p. 97 to p. 99, so this sheet is an interleaved scrap. Its drawings may or may not belong to that argument; nothing on the page ties them to it explicitly.

The printout date of 19 Aug 1982 gives a terminus post quem for the drawings, consistent with the 1983–84 dating of the dossier.

ideas.what: Sketches of discs dissected by geodesic-like chords/arcs with hatched triangular cells and marked boundary arcs, plausibly hyperbolic/conformal pictures for cutting-and-gluing ('chirurgie') of surfaces
ideas.modern_name: Geodesic triangulations / polygon decompositions of the hyperbolic disc (Klein and Poincaré models)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Poincaré); gluing surfaces from triangles appears in the dessins d'enfants literature
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses building Riemann surfaces from triangles, but these specific sketches are unpublished and uninterpretable without text

deep.surprise_reason: This is a computer-printout banner page reused as scrap, carrying only wordless sketches of dissected discs. It contains no statement or construction that can be read or attributed. Its only documentary value is the 19 Aug 1982 print date, a lower bound for when the drawings were made.
transcription_corrections: The large block characters are '0002' followed by 'FATAR'; the header reads '//* FATAR 0338 I'.
Worth recording that the page number '98' is handwritten at lower left, while the archive position is page 95 of 100.

The orange disc's chords extend beyond the circle. The lower-right thin-pen discs have thick orange boundary arcs and a hatched central triangle, and these details could be added to the figure description.
